subject: Agriculture
title: Organic in the Developing World
description: A micro-lesson that makes Organic in the Developing World usable.

hook.text: India has 2.7 million organic farmers—more than any other country. Most farm less than 2 hectares.

buildup.text: In the developing world, many small farmers already farm 'organically by default'—they can't afford chemicals.

discovery.text: Certification lets these farmers access premium export markets—European and US consumers willing to pay more.

twist.text: Certification costs and paperwork burden small farmers. Group certification through cooperatives helps, but adds complexity.

climax.text: Sikkim, an Indian state, became 100% organic in 2016—the first fully organic state in the world.

punchline.text: The world's poorest farmers may lead the organic revolution—if markets reward them.

quiz.question: Which place became the world's first fully organic state in 2016?
